results.title: Valenzuela turns empty lots into 31 parks, wins Galing Pook Award
results.description: The Valenzuela City government received a 2026 Galing Pook Award for transforming unused urban spaces into 31 public parks and recreational areas, an initiative inspired by Mayor Wes Gatchalian's childhood visits to Luneta Park in Manila. The city was named one of the 10 winners of the Galing Pook Awards for its “Building Spaces in a Spaceless City” program during the awarding ceremony at Malacañang Palace on Wednesday, Oct. 21. Gatchalian recalled growing up in a plastic manufacturing facility, where space was limited and the surroundings often felt crowded. He said his parents would occasionally take the family to Luneta, where they could play, relax, and spend time together. “Siguro, doon ko mas naunawaan kung gaano kahalaga ang magkaroon ng sariling Luneta ang isang lungsod tulad ng Valenzuela (Perhaps that was when I began to understand how important it is for a city like Valenzuela to have its own Luneta),” Gatchalian said. The mayor said those childhood experiences inspired his goal of providing residents with accessible parks and recreational spaces, regardless of their economic status. According to Gatchalian, creating these spaces, however, remains a challenge in the highly industrialized city, which has more than 20,000 factories and businesses and approximately 700,000 residents. The city has developed 31 parks and open spaces since 2015, many of them built on previously unused land. These include the Valenzuela City People's Park, Valenzuela City Family Park, Pamilyang Valenzuelano Park, and Polo Park. Through a partnership with NLEX Corporation, previously neglected spaces beneath the NLEX Harbor Link were also converted into recreational facilities, including the Valenzuela Skate Park and Paw Park. The city also developed the Valenzuela Boardwalk and Polo Riverwalk, providing a combined 7.3 kilometers of recreational spaces along flood-control structures. The Galing Pook Awards recognize local government units for innovative and effective governance programs. Gatchalian said the parks are intended not only as places for recreation but also as spaces where families and communities can spend time together. “Dito rin nabubuo ang mga pagkakaibigan, tumitibay ang samahan ng mga pamilya, at mas nararamdaman natin ang malasakit sa isa't isa (These are also places where friendships are formed, family bonds grow stronger, and people develop a greater sense of care for one another),” he said.
